DialogLine.Default: The Detapa Council does not rush into treaties. A hasty agreement is a poorly written one. Ask again later.

DialogLine.Friendly: Welcome. We are the Cardassian Union. It is a pleasure to meet a people with whom we may do business, and perhaps more.
DialogLine.Neutral: This is the Cardassian Union. We have been observing your ships. Please tell us who you are, and what you want.
DialogLine.Hostile: The Cardassian Union does not receive uninvited guests. Explain yourself, and keep it brief. The Central Command is listening.

DialogLine.Friendly: Dear friend, the Detapa Council has noted your colony in TARSYS. We are sure it was an oversight, and that you will want to correct it.
DialogLine.Neutral: SING, your colony in TARSYS lies within the Union's interests. The Obsidian Order has noticed. We suggest you reconsider.
DialogLine.Hostile: A colony in TARSYS, within Cardassian space? How very bold. Central Command has been informed. You will regret it.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your ships fired on ours, friend. We are sure there is an explanation. We would so like to hear it.
DialogLine.Neutral: You have attacked Cardassian ships, SING. The Union records every offence, and we have a very good memory.
DialogLine.Hostile: You will answer for this attack, PLURAL. The Cardassian Union does not forgive, and it does not forget.

DialogLine.Friendly: Dearest friend, your ships have remained in our space for some time. Please withdraw them, so no misunderstanding arises between us.
DialogLine.Neutral: PLURAL ships in Cardassian space. We would be most grateful if they withdrew, before the Central Command takes an interest.
DialogLine.Hostile: Your warships in Union space are an act of provocation, PLURAL. Withdraw them, or the Cardassian fleet will do it for you.

DialogLine.Friendly: We asked you to withdraw, friend, and you did not. Now you have taken TARSYS. We are very disappointed.
DialogLine.Neutral: You ignored our request and settled TARSYS. The Cardassian Union does not take kindly to being ignored, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: You trespassed, you were warned, and now you take TARSYS. Central Command will answer your insolence.

DialogLine.Friendly: You settled TARSYS and we said nothing, and now you bring warships. Our patience is not unlimited.
DialogLine.Neutral: First TARSYS, and now warships on our borders. A pattern emerges, SING, and we do not like it.
DialogLine.Hostile: You took TARSYS and now you threaten our borders. The Cardassian Union will defend itself, PLURAL. With enthusiasm.

Dialogs.DialogLine: Declare War Central Command has issued the order. The Cardassian Union is at war with you. Your worlds will learn what discipline looks like. The Obsidian Order will bring you down from within, while our fleets close in from without. It will be very orderly.>

DialogLine.Default: There are others out there? How interesting. The Obsidian Order will be delighted to hear of it. We have not yet had the pleasure.

DialogLine.Friendly: Hello, dear friend. What can the Union do to assist you? Please, do ask.
DialogLine.Neutral: Greetings, SING. We are listening. We trust this will be worth our time.
DialogLine.Hostile: Speak. Central Command is recording this conversation. Choose your words carefully.

DialogLine.Default: Your people are most interesting. We would like to know more about your history, and your customs. It is purely a matter of courtesy.
Fascinating. Central Command will find it useful.
I am afraid we do not trust you enough for this. Perhaps in time.
This is a very generous offer, from a people we barely know. We accept, naturally. We will be looking carefully at what you want in return.
This offer is poor, and we do not trust you enough to overlook it. The Union declines.
You are a valued friend, so I will be honest: your offer is not good enough. Could you try again?
A rival holds worlds in that system, and we have no open borders with them. We cannot allow your fleet to pass.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: The Union will choose its own enemies, SING. It does not need your help.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: Outsiders meddling on our borders? We find it distasteful.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: To set neighbours against each other is a poor way to repay hospitality. We expected better.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: You would have us quarrel with our neighbours? Cardassia has had enough of quarrels.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: A clever scheme. We have used most of them ourselves. We will not be used in turn.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: We see the trap, SING. It was a good attempt. We will not step into it.

DialogLine.Default: The Union's enemies hold worlds in that system, SING. We would rather your settlers were not caught up in the war.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: When the Union wants those worlds, we will take them ourselves.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: The Union does not need outsiders to settle its battlefields.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: We will not ask your settlers to risk themselves on our account. We are grateful for the thought.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: We hope to end that war, not spread it. Thank you, but no.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: Those worlds will be ours soon enough. Without your help.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: A world on the front line is a liability, not a prize. Perhaps another time.

DialogLine.Default: This offer is an insult to the Cardassian Union. We decline, and we shall remember it.
A fair arrangement. The Detapa Council approves. It is agreed.
A very good arrangement for both of us. The Council accepts.
You are far too generous, SING. We accept, and we shall remember it.
A gift for the Union? How kind. We accept, of course.
Your request is modest. The Union grants it, and trusts you will remember its kindness.
You expect the Union to bend to this? We would not push the matter, if I were you.
Very well. The Union has no wish to quarrel over so small a matter.
A poor bargain, forced upon us. The Union will remember it. The Union remembers everything.
You make a pact with the Union, and then break it? That was unwise. Central Command declares war.
So it is war. Central Command had expected it. The fleet is ready.
We are at war, PLURAL. Say what you must, and quickly.
You bring your fleet to our border, and Central Command will meet it. I do not expect a long engagement.
We warned you to leave Cardassian territory, and you stayed. Central Command has chosen war, and the fault is yours.
You remain in TARSYS despite every warning, PLURAL. The Union is at war with you.
The Union would rather not waste ships on needless wars. Perhaps a non-aggression pact would serve us both?
Excellent. The Detapa Council is pleased. The Union will honour this agreement, as long as you do.
You decline? Then we will assume that you prefer to remain open to other arrangements.
The time has come for the Cardassian Union to open its markets to you. Will you accept a trade treaty with us?
Excellent. The Council is delighted. May our trade be most profitable.
You decline trade with the Union? The Council is disappointed. As am I, SING.
First you refuse a pact, and now you ask for one? The Council does not care for indecision.
You declined trade earlier. Now you ask for it. I confess I am curious as to what has changed.
The Union requires TECH_DEMAND from you, SING. It would improve our relations.
Thank you. The Council appreciates a sensible partner.
You refuse? How unfortunate. The Obsidian Order will take note.
Your fleets appear to be in a state of disrepair and disarray. How pathetic.
Your fleet is not without merit. The Central Command has noted it, with interest.
You have improved your fleet, SING. How unfortunate. We shall have to adjust our plans.
You cannot defend your worlds, SING. The Union will take them off your hands, and bring them order.
The Borg are efficient and tireless. In many respects they are what a perfect Cardassian state might be. We admire it, from afar.
The Borg are a Collective of machines and minds. We know little of them, and we would like to keep it that way.
The Borg take whatever they wish, and leave nothing behind. We have no wish to be assimilated, and we have no intention of it.
The Dominion offers the Union security, order and a powerful friend. We are grateful for the arrangement.
The Dominion is vast and distant, and we are careful in our dealings with it. Careful, and respectful.
The Dominion's help comes at a price, and the price is our independence. Cardassia has not forgotten who it is.
The Federation is idealistic, but its people are generous. We hold them in some regard, though we would never say so to their face.
The Federation is a large and talkative union. It has not harmed us, and we have not harmed it. We remain watchful.
The Federation preaches to everyone, and listens to no one. Its Prime Directive is a polite excuse for doing nothing.
The Hydran Kingdom is a distant and respectable power. We have had no quarrel with them, and we hope to keep it so.
The Hydrans live far from our borders, and we know them only by report. We have no opinion.
The Hydrans are proud and unpredictable, and they may be dangerous. We do not pretend to understand them.
The Klingons are honest in their way, and they fight bravely. We respect that, from a safe distance.
The Klingon Empire is loud and warlike. We have no strong view of them, other than a preference for distance.
The Klingons are brutes who mistake noise for strength. They have invaded our worlds before, and they will not forget our answer.
You thought a treaty would hold the Union? Treaties are for those who cannot afford to ignore them. We can.
It is over, SING. The Cardassian Union has won. Your worlds are ours, and your people will find order very agreeable.
The PLURAL have been most agreeable, and the Council sees no harm in open borders. Shall we agree to it?
Excellent. Our ships may pass in peace, and we expect yours to do the same.
You refuse open borders? How disappointing. The Council will continue to observe you, nonetheless.
We had a treaty, and you broke it. The Union will not forget this betrayal. We are at war.
TARSYS belongs to the Union. You have invaded it. Central Command has declared war.
The Romulans are patient and disciplined, and they value secrecy. We have a good deal in common with them.
The Romulan Star Empire keeps to itself, and so do we. We find that arrangement quite agreeable.
The Romulans play deep games, and we do not trust them. They would sacrifice us for a small advantage, and without apology.

DialogLine.Friendly: Valued friend, the Cardassian Union claims the TARSYS system. Please do not go against our wishes by colonising it.
DialogLine.Neutral: TARSYS is claimed by the Cardassian Union. We suggest you look elsewhere, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: TARSYS is within the Union's claim, PLURAL. Settle there, and Central Command will remove your colony.

DialogLine.Default: TARSYS was claimed by the Union. You took it. Central Command does not overlook such things.
We have only just met the PLURAL. The Council is still forming its opinion.
The Union has no quarrel with the PLURAL. You have behaved well, and the Council takes note.
The Council has some concerns about the PLURAL. I would be happy to discuss them.
You have taken worlds that the Union had planned for itself. The Council has noticed.
You have taken worlds that the Union had planned for itself. The Council has noticed.
Your fleet has grown too large for comfort. The Council worries about such things.
Your fleet is small, and a weak neighbour is a temptation. The Council would rather not be tempted.
Your fleet is weak. The Union does not ally with those who cannot defend themselves.
Your fleet has grown too large for comfort. The Council worries about such things.
You are allied with TAREMP, who are enemies of the Union. A curious choice of friends.
You remain allied with TAREMP, who are enemies of the Union. The Order has noted it.
We have no great quarrel with you. The Council would like it to stay that way.
The war goes very well, SING. You may wish to speak while there is still someone left to hear you.
The war has not gone as Central Command hoped. I am willing to hear what you have to say, SING.
TAREMP are enemies of the Union. We invite you to join us. There will be rewards for those who help.
Excellent. The Council will be pleased. Together we shall bring TAREMP to order.
You will not help us against TAREMP? The Union will remember who stood with it.
We trusted our treaty, and you broke it. The Cardassian Union will not forget this betrayal.
Dear SING, this war has brought both sides nothing but sorrow. Won't you agree to end it?
We are winning, SING, but the Council sees no profit in prolonging it. Make peace with us.
Neither of us can win this war. A sensible people would end it before more ships are lost.
The war has gone poorly for us. The Union would accept peace, on reasonable terms.
We hold your worlds. Sign this treaty, and the Union will end the war.
You hold the field, SING. Keep your worlds, and give us peace. The Union will be patient.
You refuse peace? Then the war continues. The Union is patient.
Very well. There will be peace between us. The Council is satisfied.
A reasonable offer. The Council accepts. There will be peace.
Your offer is not good enough. The Union will not accept peace on those terms.
You still hold worlds that the Union wants. There will be no peace.
The Union will accept this peace, though it does not please us. Do not mistake it for friendship.
We were at war not long ago. The Union has not forgotten, and neither should you.
The Cardassian Union and the PLURAL understand each other so well. Perhaps it is time for a formal alliance.
Excellent. The Council welcomes this alliance, and looks forward to its fruits.
You decline an alliance with the Union? Perhaps you will think again.
This is needlessly complicated. If you want an alliance, propose one plainly.
The Council agrees. The Union will stand with you, as long as you stand with us.
An alliance? The Council has not yet decided that you deserve one.
No peace. The Union intends to finish what it has started.
There has been little loss on either side. A sensible time for peace. The Council agrees.
You will not fight beside us? Then you are no ally of the Union. The alliance is at an end.
You have crossed the Union twice now. A third time would be unwise.
You have stolen from the Union too many times. Central Command's patience is at an end.

DialogLine.DL_Agg: The Cardassian Union will defend its space and its interests with the strength they require. Our military has never been shy of doing so.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: We are a people of duty, and a proud tradition of service to the State. If you prove to be worthy of it, we will treat you accordingly.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: Cardassia has suffered greatly in the past. Our world is poor, and our people have known hunger. We wish only for a lasting peace, and the order it brings.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: The Union has survived by being more efficient and more thorough than its rivals. We intend to go on surviving.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: We are cautious with outsiders. Cardassians tend to believe that what others do not know cannot hurt us.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: The Obsidian Order sees a great deal, and says very little. It is how the Union remains so well informed.
DialogLine.DL_Exp: Cardassia's resources are meagre, and its people many. It is only natural that the Union looks outward for what it needs.
DialogLine.DL_Tech: The Union's engineers are among the best in the quadrant. Our technology is practical, efficient and thoroughly tested.
DialogLine.DL_Mil: The Cardassian fleet is disciplined, well drilled and deeply loyal. It will defend the Union against anything.
DialogLine.DL_Ind: Every Cardassian citizen has a role, and every role serves the State. Nothing is wasted. Nothing is idle.
DialogLine.DL_Gen: The Union values order, discipline and loyalty. We believe a well-ordered society can accomplish anything.

DialogLine.Default: The Vulcans are orderly, rational and reliable. We can respect a people who keep their word.
The Vulcans are cool and logical. We have no quarrel with them, and no great affection either.
The Vulcans pretend to be above us. They have watched our people suffer, and offered lectures instead of help.
We have caught you spying on us. Be warned that such actions will not be tolerated by the Cardassian Union.
We asked you to stop spying. The Obsidian Order does not ask twice.
You have spied on us again. All treaties between our peoples are cancelled.
We have captured your spy. He had a great deal to say, once he was asked properly.
We have caught on to your acts of espionage against us. Be warned that there will be consequences.
A spy among our allies? We caught your agent. Is this how the PLURAL treat friends?
You spy on us again, ally? Our alliance is at an end.
Friends should not close their borders to one another. Open yours to us, SING.
You keep your borders closed even to friends? The PLURAL are very careful.
We have only just met. The Council does not join a federation with strangers.
We are not even allies. The Council will not consider a federation until we are.
We are allies, and that is a good beginning. But a federation requires a longer history of trust.
Why should the Union follow you? We are the stronger power. If anything, you should join us.
You have proven your commitment to us through your actions. Let our combined might keep all future aggressors at bay.
Before we consider merging with you, we need you to defeat our enemies. Conquer TAREMP and the Cardassian Union will agree to merge with you.
TAREMP is destroyed. The Council is satisfied. The Union will join your federation.
You wish the Union to join your federation? The Council does not even trust you.
We will join you, but you must first ally with our friends, TAREMP. Win their confidence, and speak to us again.
You have made allies of our friends. The Council is pleased. The Union will join your federation.
You are not even at war with TAREMP. Why would the Union fight for you?
The Union is already at war with TAREMP. Were you not informed?
The Union stands with its allies. We will make war on TAREMP.
TAREMP is our ally. The Union does not break its word, even for a friend. We regret it.
Why should the Union fight for you, PLURAL? Our relations do not warrant such a favour.
Cardassia has suffered enough war. We would prefer to settle matters with TAREMP without bloodshed.
TAREMP is formidable. The Council does not choose such a war lightly. We decline.
The Cardassian Union has agreed to your war proposal. We will gladly join you. Our warships are on the way.
The Detapa Council is concerned that you cannot be trusted as an ally, SING. I hope you will correct that.
The Detapa Council has revoked our open borders. We no longer trust your empire to keep them.
